newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight - Panamaxes hold up on grain activity.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight - Panamaxes hold up on grain activity.

text.p: Chinese New Year holidays starting next Thursday are expected to reduce activity in the chartering market, but for Panamaxes at least there have been few signs so far of rates being adversely affected.
The BFI panellists marked all Panamax routes up marginally on Monday, resulting in the index gaining 7 points to 1374.

Shipbrokers heard rumours of higher US Gulf/Japan grain rates on voyage basis and, although these could not be confirmed, a significantly firmer timecharter rate was conceded by Hanjin for Hai Ji 70,083 dwt delivery US Gulf mid-Feb trip Japan at $14,500 daily plus $300,000 bonus. Also still not confirmed were reports that Cargill booked the 1974-built Cornilios 64,497 dwt prompt US Gulf for heavy grain to the Continent at a firmer $11.50/12.00.

Cargill confirmed fixing Minerva for 49,000 grains 53' Brazil/Continent for Feb 14/22 at a very economical $14.75. however grain brokers reported ore chartering enquiry emerging for second half Feb shipment from E Coast S America. Egyptian interests were linked with reports of purchases of 0.5m tonnes from E.U. for March/April loading. Egyptian charterers were active from Australia - the Panamax newbuilding Torm Martha being reported fixed delivery ex yard Japan redelivery Damietta at $7,000 daily, and Torm Tekla 69,268 dwt delivery Chiba redelivery Port Said northbound at $7,300 daily, both for loading Australian grain.

Some period timecharter business was also seen - Hanjin were linked with Anangel Argonaut 65,668 dwt delivery Japan end Feb for 5-7 months at $9,750 daily, and Halla took Daiten 69,497 dwt delivery Japan March/April for 1 option 1 year at $10,650 and $11,500 daily respectively. In the Atlantic Frapaco were said to have booked United Hope 69,011 dwt delivery UK mid March for 7-9 or 9-11 months at $10,250 daily with a bonus of $225,000 if redelivery Far East.

Among new grain orders quoted Monday were 30,100 wheat St Lawrence/Seaforth Feb 20/25 (European grain), 30,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Indonesia Feb 25/march 8 (Cho Yang), 25,000 heavy grain Up River/2 Spanish Med Feb 12/24 (Cargill), and 600/700,000 CFT grain Gulf/Ireland Feb 20/28 and 15,000 barley Rostock/Libya Feb 12/17 (both Toepfer).

Rohstoffhandel's fixture of 150,000 ironore Tubarao/Rotterdam for end Feb at $5.75 represented a further decline in the Atlantic Caper market. Protector 2 was believed fixed by Mega Pacific for 90,000 tonnes Tubarao/Bahrein for Feb 15/28, but the rate remained private. Ankerkolen were linked with Commander for 110,000 coal Richards Bay/Ijmuiden and Amsterdam for April loading in the high $6.00's, but many believed the business failed on subjects. Lalemant were rumoured to have fixed Konavle for 70,000 ironore Tubarao/Ghent for Feb 15/28 in the high $8.00's, and British Steel may have booked 65,000 coal Dalrple/Immingham for early March at about $11.00, but confirmation was lacking.
